visual_description: A close-up of a weather-beaten yellow field notebook. The left page features a meticulous graphite sketch of a 3-foot dinosaur horn pedestalized in rock. The right page contains tight, legible technical handwriting. A small photo-scale bar is taped to the bottom of the page.

content_declaration.rock_stratification: Located in a distinct 40cm thick lens of cross-bedded fluvial sandstone, situated 12 meters below the K-Pg boundary layer (iridium anomaly).
content_declaration.matrix_material: Medium-grained, poorly sorted 'salt-and-pepper' sandstone. High carbonaceous content with visible leaf impressions (Ficus) in the surrounding silt stringers.

constraints.visual_note: Handwriting should include small 'strike-throughs' or corrections to feel authentic to field conditions.
constraints.background: The notebook is resting on a pair of dusty work gloves (Tan leather).
